title: BMC infeasibility explanation benchmark run
description: The shape of one immutable run under outputs/runs/<run-id>/. This is benchmark output and is deliberately NOT part of the public BMC result schema: it may change whenever the measurement map changes, and no consumer of pyfcstm results should read it.

manifest.description: manifest.json: everything a reader needs to know what was measured, on what, and whether the tree was clean.

schema.description: Renaming or removing a field requires a new version.

run_id.description: Directory name. A saved run is never overwritten; a correction creates a new id.

commit.description: Full commit. A short prefix cannot identify a revision later.

arms.description: The contrast, in comparison order: baseline, none, formal, proof.

warmups.description: Discarded runs. Kept separate because the first run of a sample pays costs no later run repeats.

z3.description: "unavailable" when the solver could not be imported, so a run without it is not mistaken for one whose version went unrecorded.

dirty.description: A run from a dirty tree is still recorded, but says so.

inputs.description: Digest per corpus file, over line-ending-normalized text so checkouts agree.

source.description: The field or instrument the number comes from.

note.description: What the timing boundary includes. proof_construction covers construction and derived-side rule checking together; they are not separable in the production ledger.

summary.description: summary.json: one entry per case, each holding one entry per arm. Rebuildable from raw.jsonl.

expected_depth.description: What this case is in the corpus to exercise.

failures.description: Failed samples are counted and reported, not dropped.

peak_child_rss_bytes.description: High-water mark of the child process. null when psutil was unavailable; never 0, which would read as a measurement.

stages_p50_ms.description: Per-stage medians. proof_linearization is benchmark-only instrumentation, not a ledger entry.

unstable_fields.description: Published fields that varied across repetitions. Instability is a finding, so it is surfaced rather than collapsed.
